# Independent audit: critical zero-endpoint support facets

Audited all four sections of
`candidate 568f7cf028ec23b6`.

**Result: PASS.**

## One-sided support-face derivative

After orthogonal coordinates, the perturbed plane is exactly
s>=-epsilon(a.r+c)/(||u||+epsilon*b), with positive denominator for
small epsilon. Boundedness gives one uniform O(epsilon) slab and one
bounded tangential projection. At every fixed tangential point outside
the support-face projection, compactness supplies a strictly negative
vertical upper endpoint, so its divided captured length eventually
vanishes. At almost every point in the relative interior of a facet,
the vertical interval extends below zero. To make the latter explicit,
fix a small relative ball in the facet around that point and one interior
body point below the plane; a sufficiently small interpolation can adjust
the face point within that ball so that the resulting point has precisely
the original tangential coordinate. This supplies a vertical segment.

The divided lengths are uniformly bounded, so dominated convergence
applies. Facet boundaries have zero (d-1)-measure; if the whole support
face has smaller dimension, its entire projection is null instead. The
result is exactly the integral of the positive affine part divided by
||u||. A strict support gap leaves the perturbed cap empty for small
epsilon. No smoothness or facet-preservation assumption is hidden.

The proper-cut signed derivative follows from the same bounded difference
quotient. Almost every point of the relative section interior is an
interior point of the full-dimensional body and has a vertical interval
on both sides. Points outside that section have a fixed local gap. This
justifies the claimed signed integral for nonsmooth bodies as well.

## Criticality signs and capacities

At base -1 the affine perturbation is w.(x-y)-beta; at base zero it is
w.(x-y); at base +1 it is w.(x-y)+beta. Thus every sign and coefficient
in the full directional inequality is correct. All these perturbations
keep the actual source on the boundary, and the original continuous
normal stays nonzero for sufficiently small perturbations. A local
minimum therefore gives the one-sided inequality for every w,beta.

A zero captured volume in a full-dimensional body implies the original
body lies on the noncaptured side. If its cut is strictly beyond support,
beta=1,w=0 gives the impossible derivative -sigma_A. At support the same
choice gives sigma_A<=H_(d-1)(F_B). Since sigma_A>0, an actual facet is
necessary. Lower-dimensional support faces cannot satisfy the condition.
The entire facet distribution remains in the continuous-normal terms;
the proof does not freely assign its centroid.

The actual section midpoint inclusion is valid because the three
thresholds have their exact affine relation. All section planes are
parallel; translating them into u^perp preserves surface measure and the
midpoint inclusion. Ordinary (d-1)-dimensional BM applies to the two
positive-area section bodies and yields sigma_K>=sigma_A. The explicit
d>=2 hypothesis correctly excludes an undefined zero-dimensional root.

## Simultaneous zero-capture normalization

For the full-rank d+1 positive circuit, every margin is strictly negative
at each interior point of B. Their weighted sum is the integer drift D,
so D<0. Positive rescaling by (d+1)lambda_i/(-D) gives sum v_i=0 and
sum t_i=-(d+1), without changing any cap.

The map s->(v_i.s)_i has rank d and image exactly the zero-sum hyperplane.
The target entries -1-t_i sum to zero, so the asserted unique s exists.
Substituting x-y=x'+s*z transforms each margin into v_i.x'-z, confirming
both the shear sign and the normalized cap inequality. The shear fixes
integer bases and translates each continuous fiber, so the mixed lattice,
fiber volumes, halfspace family, and criticality are preserved.

Zero B captures put B inside all v_i.x'<=1. The map
x'->((1-v_i.x')/(d+1)) is an affine bijection onto sum lambda_i=1;
nonnegative coordinates describe the standard simplex. This proves T is
an actual full-dimensional bounded simplex and its centroid is zero.
It does NOT show 0 in B or B=T, exactly as the source cautions.

Proper A indices give actual supporting facets of this SAME B body,
with its transformed section at level +1, the A section at -1, and the
K section at zero. The section inclusions and capacities survive the
fiber translations. Saturated A cuts remain explicitly outside the
proper-cut assertion.

No correction is needed.

## A verified equality consequence of the full variation

If the proper-A row has sigma_A=H_(d-1)(F_B)=m, then its directional
inequality forces the exact centroid identity

    m(c_A-y)+sigma_K(c_K-y)+m(c_FB-y)=0.                 (1)

For any fixed w choose beta sufficiently large that w.(x-y)+beta>0 for
all x in the compact facet F_B. The facet integral is then linear and
its beta term cancels -m beta from the A section. The remaining
inequality is w dotted with the left side of (1), nonnegative. Repeating
with -w and another sufficiently large beta proves equality for every w.

If additionally sigma_K=m, then the actual section midpoint inclusion
and section BM force equality throughout. For q=d-1>=2, the positive-volume
BM equality case and equal endpoint q-volumes make the two endpoint
sections translates; for q=1 equal-length intervals have this property
directly. Their midpoint has volume m, so its inclusion in the middle
section of volume m is equality. Hence c_K=(c_A+c_FB)/2. Substituting this
in (1) gives 3m(c_K-y)=0 and therefore y=c_K.

This conclusion is conditional on both displayed area equalities. It does
not replace the general facet integral by an arbitrarily chosen centroid.
